protocol: D-000 turn 2 of 3, same cycle as turn 1; refute not confirm; RULE-GOVERNED recording of gate-harness-naming.v3 plus operative rider RB-GHN-V3-A1
summary: My turn-1 SHOULD-FIX landed exactly as proposed, the arithmetic is untouched and still closes, and all five substantive pins now match live bytes including the re-measured COORD. But the subject was dispatched unfinished. It ends with seven lines of the coordinator's own working notes, in the first person, instructing itself to fix the file before finishing it — and those notes are correct: the 'Codex turn 1' digest is D-087's Codex verdict, not D-086's. I confirmed that independently by hashing both files without opening either. A third defect is in the disposition table, which says clause 3 'already' named both denominators and that no edit was made; the diff against the frozen turn-1 subject shows clause 3 was edited in precisely the way the note asked.

objections.location: Subject, lines 119-125, following the 'Measured inputs at turn-2 dispatch' table
objections.claim: The frozen subject ends with the coordinator's unfinished working notes, which are not decision text and which declare the file incomplete.
objections.why: The seven trailing lines read 'Wait - Codex turn 1 D-086 hash is not fafcaf48 (that's D-087). I need the D-086 Codex hash.', 'D-086 Codex file: was 6662 bytes. Need hash of frozen D-086 codex verdict.', 'I chmod'd it. Hash it before finishing this file. I accidentally put D-087's codex hash.', and 'Let me hash D-086 codex and fix the draft. I wrote the file already with the wrong hash. Fix it.' The file also has no terminating newline, which is the signature of an interrupted write rather than a finished document. This is disqualifying on two independent grounds. First, a D-000 subject is adopted into COORD as written, so this first-person editorial matter would enter the permanent decision record verbatim. Second, the notes are a statement by the author that the artifact is not finished — 'Hash it before finishing this file', 'I wrote the file already with the wrong hash. Fix it.' — and a document that says of itself that it still needs fixing cannot be the frozen object of a review turn. Turn 2 is one turn from adoption; this must not reach turn 3 in this state.
objections.repair: Delete lines 119-125 in full, terminate the file with a newline, and re-dispatch at a new digest.

objections.location: Subject, 'Measured inputs at turn-2 dispatch' table, row 'Codex turn 1'
objections.claim: The pinned Codex turn-1 digest belongs to a different entry's verdict.
objections.why: The row pins fafcaf48c39bc1a146a0adf48d00bfaac9c51e7487a6407418d39d31151aa385. I hashed both candidate files without opening either: that value is coordinator-decisions.D-087.review-adversarial.codex.json, 6914 bytes. The D-086 Codex turn-1 verdict is coordinator-decisions.D-086.review-adversarial.codex.json and hashes to f58dfd6395ae9300558367f1bded888c2a61a91f5969871dbba7de4b0ede6dff at 6662 bytes — the same 6662 the coordinator's own note cites. So the entry pins the wrong reviewer verdict for the other reviewer's turn-1 position, and the mis-pinned file is the neighbouring entry I reviewed immediately before this one. I record that I established this by hashing, not by reading: the contents of neither Codex verdict were opened. This is not excused by the trailing note admitting it. The note is not a correction — the table still carries the wrong value, and the subject was frozen and dispatched in that state. It is also the precise defect class D-080 exists to remedy, that entry having been created solely to correct a mis-cited Codex verdict digest, which makes an uncorrected instance of it in a frozen subject a repeat rather than a novelty.
objections.repair: Replace the 'Codex turn 1' value with f58dfd6395ae9300558367f1bded888c2a61a91f5969871dbba7de4b0ede6dff and re-dispatch.

objections.location: Subject, disposition table, row D086-N-1: 'RECORDED. Clause 3 already names both denominators: owners 22 of 22 gate rows; named-harness half 0 of 18 required. No edit.'
objections.claim: The disposition misstates both the prior text and the entry's own change: clause 3 did not already name the denominators, and it was edited.
objections.why: I diffed the turn-2 subject against the frozen turn-1 subject rather than relying on either document's account of itself. Turn 1 clause 3 reads 'Owners remain 22 of 22. Named-harness half remains 0 of 18 in file 08'. Turn 2 clause 3 reads 'Owners remain 22 of 22 gate rows. Named-harness half remains 0 of 18 required gates in file 08'. The words 'gate rows' and 'required gates' are additions made at turn 2, and they are exactly the denominator-naming my note asked for. So the substance is right and the note is answered well — the defect is confined to the record of what happened. 'Already' is false of the turn-1 text, and 'No edit' is false of the diff. That matters because the disposition table is the entry's account of how it responded to review, and it is the artifact a later reader consults to reconstruct what each turn changed. An entry that improves its text and simultaneously records that it changed nothing makes its own change history unreliable.
objections.repair: Restate the disposition as accepted-and-edited, for example: 'ACCEPTED. Clause 3 now names both denominators: owners 22 of 22 gate rows; named-harness half 0 of 18 required gates. Edited from the turn-1 wording.'

notesNonBlocking.location: Subject, 'Measured inputs at turn-2 dispatch' section
notesNonBlocking.observation: Turn 1 closed its measured-inputs table with 'If a cited file moves, re-measure. Do not edit this subject after dispatch.' Turn 2 drops both sentences and adds no replacement, which I confirmed by diff and by a zero-match search for the clause. I record this because that clause did real work at turn 1: it is the reason I cleared the stale COORD pin as anticipated movement rather than raising it as a false pin. The removal falsifies nothing, since the heading 'Measured inputs at turn-2 dispatch' carries its own temporal qualifier and the freeze is enforced by the dispatch and by file mode. But COORD will move again the moment D-086 is itself adopted, so the entry will carry a stale COORD pin with no provision telling a later reader that this is expected. Restoring the one sentence costs nothing.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 07e7c5aa21fef32d2b36bf4014ea826c1d6cb20b473180c69335faf229295369, three measurements each, equal to the dispatched value, -r--r--r-- at both ends. Prompt held at 6583a52c… across start and end.
The attack 'turn-1 subject edited' fails. It measures 49732971… at start and at end, unchanged from turn 1 and equal to the value the turn-2 subject itself pins for it.

The attack 'D086-SF-1 not landed' fails, and the repair is the one I asked for rather than a paraphrase of it. The rider now reads 'Remove the word "countable" from that sentence only. The refusals in v3's authorityClaim and whatThisDoesNotDo that name "countable required" in order to forbid it are retained verbatim.' Both the scoping and the explicit preservation of the two refusals are present, and the entry adds a matching rejected alternative, 'Leave "Remove the word countable" unscoped. Rejected: D086-SF-1.' The unscoped sentence is gone from the subject.
The entry's account of my turn-1 verdict is exact — 'Claude 2 OBJECT, 0 MUST-FIX, 1 SHOULD-FIX D086-SF-1, 1 NOTE D086-N-1' matches the file I wrote, which hashes to 6365e0b9… as the table pins.

The attack 'presents 16 of 16 as the required denominator' still fails. I diffed clause 2 against turn 1 and it is byte-identical, so the arithmetic I rebuilt at turn 1 from D-002 and from v3's gate records — nineteen minus G17 order-equal to v3's eighteen, eighteen minus {G03, G04} equal to sixteen — carries over untouched. Clause 3 still reads '16 of 18, not 16 of 16, and still not MET', now with both denominators named.

The attacks 'counts G03/G04 as named' and 'restores G17 as required-now' still fail: clause 2 is unchanged, the header still refuses to pin G03/G04 machines and to restore SARIF or G17, and both rejected alternatives survive at 'Count G03/G04 as named. Rejected: GHN-V1-B2' and 'Restore G17. Rejected: D-077.'

The attack 'this entry itself writes file 08 or claims condition 4 MET' fails. file 08 measures ff2ebadd…, matching the pin, and git reports it unmodified in my working tree. Condition 4 stays PARTLY MET in clause 3 and in the readiness effect, and turn 2 strengthens the readiness effect by adding 'Condition 5 remains NOT MET and last.'

The attack 'silent SATISFIED / QUALIFIED / DEMONSTRATED' fails on a line-by-line audit of the turn-2 text. Every occurrence is a refusal or an unchanged standing: SATISFIED negated three times, QUALIFIED and DEMONSTRATED both inside 'Does not claim', and the MET occurrences are 'Does not make condition 4 MET', 'stays PARTLY MET' twice, 'still not MET' and 'Condition 5 remains NOT MET'. No status token is coined or elevated.

The attack 'authorizes docs/v2/implementation/' fails: both occurrences are refusals, the rejected alternative 'Authorize implementation. Rejected: condition 5 remains last' survives, and the directory does not exist.

The attack 'cited digests do not match live bytes' fails for every substantive input, and the COORD re-measure the prompt claims is real. COORD now pins 236a97fa…, which equals live bytes and is the post-D-087 value I supplied at turn 1; file 08 ff2ebadd…, v3 b5236612…, my v3 verdict ba7f48c3… and the Codex v3 verdict b5162d99… all match, the last hashed without opening. Both commits resolve: 75c981dd… to D-056 and 953b2311… to 'D-087: remove duplicate D-056 heading'. The single failing row is the Codex turn-1 verdict, raised above.
The two new adoption claims are true: D-087 is adopted at 953b2311… and present in COORD, and D-086 is still absent from COORD, so adoption creates no collision.
No turn-2 Codex verdict file exists at review time, so there was nothing for me to avoid opening on that side; the turn-1 Codex verdict I hashed without opening.
I wrote one file, the verdict named for me, and edited and committed nothing. The frozen turn-1 subject, file 08 and COORD are all unmodified in my working tree.
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex reviews of D-086 at either turn. I may not read them. I hashed the turn-1 file at f58dfd63… without opening it, which is how I established that the pinned value belongs to a different entry — I did not read either file's contents to reach that conclusion. The entry's claim that Codex returned CONSENT with 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX at turn 1 is therefore unverified by me.
The Codex review of v3, and therefore the actual wording of GHN-V3-A1. As at turn 1, I verified the rider's effect on v3's bytes, not its fidelity to the advisory it claims to implement.
Whether each proposed harness identifier is the right name for its gate's work.
Whether any gate's standing has been overtaken by an adopted decision later than D-077.
The merits of D-035, D-042, D-056, D-077 and D-087 themselves. I verified existence, form and the operative content cited, not their correctness.

objectionNote: I OBJECT with two MUST-FIX and one SHOULD-FIX. The decision itself is in good shape: my turn-1 finding was accepted in the exact form I proposed, the note was answered with a real improvement, the arithmetic is byte-identical to the version I rebuilt from source, and the COORD pin was properly re-measured. What fails is the artifact, not the reasoning. The subject was frozen and dispatched with the coordinator's working notes still attached, and those notes say in plain terms that the file needs fixing before it is finished — which is not a state a review turn can consent to, one turn from adoption. The mis-pinned Codex digest is real and I confirmed it by hashing rather than by taking the note's word for it, and it is worth saying that the wrong file is the neighbouring entry's Codex verdict: this is the D-080 defect class recurring. Both repairs are mechanical. The disposition row is the subtler one — the entry made the right edit and then recorded that it made none, and the change history is the thing a later reader has to trust.
